records.title: Pancreatic islet cryopreservation by vitrification achieves high viability, function, recovery and clinical scalability for transplantation
records.abstract: Pancreatic islet transplantation can cure diabetes but requires accessible, high-quality islets in sufficient quantities. Cryopreservation could solve islet supply chain challenges by enabling quality-controlled banking and pooling of donor islets. Here, vitrification and rewarming optimization achieved high post-thaw viability, preserved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, and strong transplant performance across mouse, porcine, human, and stem cell-derived beta cell islets.

records.title: Nanowarming of vitrified pancreatic islets as a cryopreservation technology for transplantation
records.abstract: Biobanking of pancreatic islets for transplantation could solve donor shortages, but large-volume rewarming remains a bottleneck because slow warming causes devitrification. This study showed that magnetic nanoparticle-based nanowarming improved viability of vitrified mouse islets in larger volumes and supported glucose control after transplantation into diabetic mice.
records.authorsFlat: Taisei Wakabayashi; Masahiro Kaneko; Tomoki Nakai; Masanobu Horie; Hiroyuki Fujimoto; Masazumi Takahashi; Shota Tanoue; Akira Ito

records.title: The effect of hydroxyethyl starch as a cryopreservation agent during freezing of mouse pancreatic islets
records.abstract: Dimethyl sulfoxide is the standard penetrating cryoprotective agent for islet freezing but has substantial toxicity. This study compared hydroxyethyl starch formulations against DMSO and found improved recovery, viability, and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion after mouse islet cryopreservation, with reduced apoptosis and necrosis markers.
records.authorsFlat: Du Yeon Shin; Jae Suh Park; Han-Sin Lee; Wooyoung Shim; Lauren Jin; Kyo Won Lee; Jae Berm Park; Dong Hyun Kim; Jae Hyeon Kim

records.rawQuery: site:pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov pancreatic islet trehalose cryopreservation transplantation
records.title: Reviving hope: unlocking pancreatic islet immortality by optimizing a trehalose-based cryopreservation media and cell-penetrating peptide
records.abstract: This study evaluated trehalose with a poly L proline cell-penetrating peptide as a cryopreservation system for rat pancreatic islets. Frozen-thawed islets preserved viability, insulin and glucagon staining, glucose-responsive insulin secretion, and transplantation efficacy in diabetic mice, suggesting a credible alternative cryomix for islet banking.
records.authorsFlat: Zakieh Samsonchi; Roshanak Amirian; Lobat Tayebi; Hossein Derakhshankhah; Zhila Izadi; Ensiyeh Hajizadeh-Saffar
